title: Λάρος καὶ ἰκτῖνος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 193. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Λάρος ἰχθὺν καταπιών, διαρραγέντος αὐτῷ τοῦ φάρυγγος, ἐπὶ τῆς ἠιόνος νεκρὸς ἔκειτο.
sentences.tr: Laros ichthyn katapiōn, diarragentos autōi tou pharyngos, epi tēs ēionos nekros ekeito.
sentences.l: A gull, having gulped down a fish, his gullet having been torn open, lay dead upon the shore.
sentences.i: A gull gulped down a fish, his gullet burst, and he lay dead on the shore.
sentences.n: διαρραγέντος … τοῦ φάρυγγος is a genitive absolute, with αὐτῷ the dative of the person concerned: the throat that burst was his own. καταπίνω is to swallow whole, straight down. In ἠιόνος the η and the ι are two separate vowels (the word is ἠϊών, the shore), so the romanized ēi here is not the iota subscript it marks elsewhere.

sentences.t: Ἰκτῖνος δὲ αὐτὸν θεασάμενος ἔφη· « Ἄξια σύ γε πέπονθας, ὅτι πτηνὸν γεννηθεὶς ἐπὶ θαλάσσης τὴν δίαιταν ἐποιοῦ. »
sentences.tr: Iktinos de auton theasamenos ephē· « Axia sy ge peponthas, hoti ptēnon gennētheis epi thalassēs tēn diaitan epoiou. »
sentences.l: And a kite, having beheld him, said: « You for your part have suffered what you deserved, because, having been born a winged creature, you made your living upon the sea. »
sentences.i: And a kite, seeing him, said: « You have got no more than your deserts, since you were born a bird and made your living on the sea. »
sentences.n: ἄξια πάσχειν is to suffer what matches what one has done. γε narrows it to him: you at any rate. δίαιταν ποιεῖσθαι is to make one's way of life, hence to get one's living, and ἐποιοῦ is the second person of the imperfect middle. πτηνὸν γεννηθείς sets the whole complaint: born a thing of the air, not of the water.

sentences.t: Οὕτως οἱ τὰ οἰκεῖα ἐπιτηδεύματα καταλιπόντες καὶ τοῖς μηδὲν προσήκουσιν ἐπιβαλλόμενοι εἰκότως δυστυχοῦσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtōs hoi ta oikeia epitēdeumata katalipontes kai tois mēden prosēkousin epiballomenoi eikotōs dystychousin.
sentences.l: So those who abandon their own pursuits and set themselves upon things that in no way belong to them, with good reason come off badly.
sentences.n: ἐπιτήδευμα is a man's regular occupation, the thing he practises. προσήκω is to belong to, to be one's proper concern, and μηδέν is adverbial, "in no respect". εἰκότως is "as one would expect" — the misfortune is not bad luck but the natural sequel.
